govdocs-archive_org-julius-evola-tao-te-: Julius Evola’s commentary on the Tao Te Ching reads Laozi through the traditionalist lens. The Italian thinker’s terse pages distill the old Chinese wisdom. Each note rewards slow reading. The Way unfolds in his hands. The book is a gem of traditionalist thought.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-ArmstrongJohn_J: This item — nsia-ArmstrongJohn: John Armstrong — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of the archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-Bugging_Bugging: This Center for National Security Studies mailing — on bugging — is a civil-liberties mailer. The file belongs to the political archive. The Center fought surveillance abuses. Mailings rallied the members. The 1970s were the heyday. The item is a fragment of advocacy history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-GervaisPershing: Rosemary James’s Pershing Gervais Talks From His Unknown Hideaway covers the Garrison aide’s flight. Gervais fled the probe’s fallout. The interview was a scoop. He spoke from hiding. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-ImmunityCongres: Timothy J. Robinson’s Appellate Court Limits Immunity of Hill Aides is a Washington Post piece. The ruling curbed congressional cover. Aides lost their shield. The decision mattered. The file belongs to the legal archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-KleinsSportingG: This letter to Gary Mack — October 20, 1984, creator unknown — is a researcher’s note. Mack was the Dallas researcher. The letter may hold a clue. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-LaneMarkMLKing_: Mark Lane’s The Reason for the Book is the author’s defense. Lane was the first Warren Commission critic. His book was Rush to Judgment. The defense is spirited. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of publishing history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-NorthAdvertisin: Charles Nicodemus’s NRA vs. North Advertising is a press piece. The gun lobby fought its ad agency. The feud made headlines. The piece is a time capsule. The file belongs to the business archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-ParkTonsung_Par: Maxine Cheshire’s Tongsun Park and the Korean CIA is a Washington Post piece. Park bribed congressmen in the Koreagate scandal. The scandal rocked Washington. The piece endures. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
himalayan-journals-volume-1-or-notes-of-: Botanist Joseph Dalton Hooker — Darwin's closest scientific friend — spent years exploring the Himalayas, and these journals are his record. This first volume follows his travels through Bengal and Sikkim, collecting plants at altitudes no European naturalist had reached. Vivid, observant, and adventurous, it is a classic of scientific travel writing.
himalayan-journals-complete-or-notes-of-: This complete edition gathers Joseph Dalton Hooker's full account of his pioneering botanical expeditions through the eastern Himalayas. Across Bengal, Sikkim, and Nepal he documented thousands of plants — many new to science — while braving some of the world's toughest mountain travel. A landmark of nineteenth-century natural history, blending science with high adventure.
himalayan-journals-volume-2-or-notes-of-: Joseph Dalton Hooker's second volume carries his Himalayan expedition deeper into Sikkim and toward Nepal. More high-altitude plant hunting, more encounters with mountain peoples, and more of Hooker's sharp scientific eye on a world few Europeans had seen. Together with the first volume, it stands as one of the great botanical adventures of the nineteenth century.
fruit-gathering: Rabindranath Tagore, the Bengali poet who won the Nobel Prize in 1913, gathers short poems of love, nature, and spiritual longing in this collection. Each piece is brief — a single ripe thought, like fruit picked at its moment. Translated into Tagore's own beautiful English, the poems carry the gentle wisdom that made him beloved around the world.
fielding: Austin Dobson profiles Henry Fielding — novelist of Tom Jones, playwright, and London magistrate — in this volume of the English Men of Letters series. Dobson's elegant, sympathetic study captures the gusto and humanity of the great eighteenth-century writer. A model literary biography, concise and full of life.
the-social-cancer-a-complete-english-ver: José Rizal's Noli Me Tangere — The Social Cancer — is the great novel of the Philippines, exposing Spanish colonial cruelty through the story of Crisóstomo Ibarra. Its publication in 1887 ignited the movement for Filipino freedom; Rizal himself was executed for his writings. A masterpiece of political fiction and a nation's founding book.
school-and-home-cooking: Carlotta Greer's textbook taught generations of students the science and art of cooking — nutrition, technique, and household management in clear lessons. Tested recipes and practical guidance made it a classroom staple. A fascinating record of how home economics was once taught.
back-to-billabong: Mary Grant Bruce brings her beloved Norah back to Billabong — the great Australian cattle station — for new adventures in the bush. Kangaroos, riders, and station life fill these sunny pages. Australia's favorite children's series at its most delightful. Bush rides, station fun, and the loyal Norah make this a sunlit favorite of Australian childhood.
mankind-in-the-making: H. G. Wells turns sociologist in this bold, provocative book on education and the future of the race. How should children be raised, and schools be shaped, to build a better world? Wells answers with his usual vigor, vision, and impatience with the old. A fascinating piece of Edwardian futurism.
on-something: Hilaire Belloc muses on something — anything, everything — in these delightful essays. His wide-ranging talk covers inns, Sussex, and the human lot. Vintage Belloc, various and vigorous. His talk ranges from cheese to Christendom with equal gusto. No topic is too small for his large and lively mind.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alms-and-alms: This 1913 reference piece on alms and almsgiving — the Church's law of charity. James David O'Neill sets out its duty. The poor have a claim on our goods. Mercy covers a multitude of sins. The Gospel's golden command. Its practice marks the Lenten season.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apostolic-ble: A 1913 entry on the apostolic blessing — the dying's plenary indulgence. Frederick Holweck explains its tender use. The priest imparts it at the last hour. The Church speeds the parting soul. The final blessing of the faith. Its form is short and tender.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-augustine-red: This 1913 reference piece on Augustine Reding — the Prince-Abbot of Einsiedeln. Michael Ott honors his learned rule. His abbey's library grew under him. The Swiss Church knew his sway. A mitred scholar of the Alps. His Theologia defended the old school.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-benedictine-a: A 1913 entry on Kilwinning Abbey — the Ayrshire house of the monks. Oswald Hunter-Blair notes its medieval glory. Its tower crowns the old town. The Reformation ended its prayer. A jewel of the Scottish west. Its arch is all that stands.
